title: American Airlines Restoring Seat-Back Screens to 800+ Planes in Major Cabin Overhaul
excerpt: The airline is reversing its decade-old strategy and adding premium seats as it tries to close a profitability gap with Delta and United.
body:
• American Airlines will retrofit more than 800 narrowbody aircraft with seatback entertainment screens by the early 2030s, reversing its previous strategy of removing them
  • Premium seating will increase to 40% of narrowbody departures, up from 25%, as premium travelers already generate nearly half of ticketed revenue
  • The overhaul includes Starlink Wi-Fi, more first-class seats, and extra-legroom options — but American still trails Delta and United in profitability

American Airlines announced Tuesday it will add seatback entertainment screens to more than 800 narrowbody aircraft and significantly expand premium seating across its domestic fleet, stepping up its bid for higher-spending travelers as it tries to narrow a wide profitability gap with rivals Delta Air Lines and United Airlines.

The move marks a stark reversal for the carrier, which began ripping screens out of its planes nearly a decade ago, betting that passengers would stream content on their own devices. That bet did not pay off.

Screens Come Back

American said customer preferences have shifted, particularly among younger travelers who increasingly want access to larger screens alongside their own devices, according to Reuters. Advances in high-speed satellite Wi-Fi have also made a more connected and personalized onboard experience possible.

Retrofits will begin in 2028 and are expected to be completed in the early 2030s. New Airbus and Boeing aircraft with the screens built in will also begin arriving that year. American already has more than 140 widebody and Airbus A321XLR aircraft equipped with seatback screens. The carrier declined to disclose how much the program will cost.

"We are excited to introduce our refreshed interiors and new premium seats on our narrowbody aircraft, offering our customers more space to stow their carry-ons and a convenient way to power their devices."

— Heather Garboden, American Airlines Chief Customer Officer

The airline had previously announced plans to add Starlink Wi-Fi on hundreds of narrowbody planes starting next year, according to the Wall Street Journal.

Premium Push

American said premium seating would rise to about 40% of seats on narrowbody departures in coming years, up from roughly 25% today. The airline is adding more first-class seats and main cabin seats with extra legroom as aircraft are reconfigured and new jets join the fleet.

The carrier is retrofitting its Airbus A319 and A320 fleets to add an extra row in first class. Its A321neo fleet will be reconfigured for more first-class seating, and upcoming deliveries of Boeing 737 MAX 10 planes will feature two dozen first-class seats. Premium travelers generated nearly half of American's ticketed revenue in the second quarter while accounting for roughly 30% of seats.

The refreshed A319 and A320 cabins will also include larger overhead bins, USB-C power at every seat, mood lighting, and privacy wings on premium seats — bringing them closer to the interiors on American's new Boeing 787-9 and A321XLR aircraft, according to Business Traveller.

Closing the Gap

Despite the upgrades, American continues to trail Delta and United in profitability. CEO Robert Isom last week shook up senior management and acknowledged a "meaningful gap" between American's performance and where it should be. Flight attendants earlier this year called for a leadership change, while the pilots union has questioned whether current management can deliver results.

American expects roughly break-even results this year, while Delta and United have forecast solid profits. The pressure is on Isom to show the premium strategy can deliver.

What It Means for US–India Travelers

For the millions of passengers who fly between the US and India — or who use American's domestic network to connect — the changes signal a significantly improved experience ahead. The combination of seatback screens, Starlink Wi-Fi, and more premium options on domestic legs could make American a stronger competitor on connecting itineraries to India, where long-haul comfort already relies on the airline's widebody fleet. But with retrofits not beginning until 2028, the improvements are still years away from reaching most flights.
